channel.title: The Center For Michigan | Bridge Magazine - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Center For Michigan | Bridge Magazine (thecenterformichigan.net)

item.title: Michigan quietly kills effort to restructure mental health care system
item.description: The decision follows a judge’s order to block the state’s request for proposal. The state says its aim in seeking bidders was to introduce ‘consumer choice’ to the Medicaid-backed system.

item.title: In Michigan Senate race, Dems battle for bucks as Mike Rogers builds war chest
item.description: Six months from the primary and with no clear frontrunner for the Democratic nomination, fundraising remains tight in Michigan’s closely-watched US Senate race.

item.title: Opinion | Water affordability fund would help close Michigan investment gap
item.description: Michigan needs $85 billion in investment over 20 years to bring its water and wastewater systems in line. An affordability plan before lawmakers can not only support residents facing shutoffs, but water systems as well.

item.title: Michigan sends message to 80,000 high school students: Take AP classes
item.description: High school students with a high score on pre-SAT tests are being encouraged to get on track for college.

item.title: Opinion | MSU must return what they took — and add more
item.description: There is now zero legal justification — not even the pretense of pending litigation — for Michigan State University to dismantle equity programs. Yet MSU continues operating as if the Trump administration’s unconstitutional orders carry force of law.

item.title: Federal food assistance changes taking $95M bite out of Michigan budget
item.description: President Donald Trump’s ‘big, beautiful’ law will mean a big new expense for Michigan, which will be required to pay a larger share of administrative costs for federal food assistance.

item.title: Where Michigan gubernatorial candidates stand on data centers
item.description: Bridge Michigan asked gubernatorial candidates for their stance on the hot-button issue of data centers, amid concerns surrounding Benson’s familial and professional connections to a data center developer. Here’s what they said.

item.title: Data center moratoriums pile up in Michigan. No one knows if they’ll work
item.description: No fewer than 19 communities have paused data center development, while bipartisan lawmakers push to repeal policies that have lured the industry to Michigan.

item.title: St. Clair County makes it easier for parents to opt out of vaccines
item.description: The health department announced a streamlined approach Monday to expedite vaccine waivers and reminded families they can opt out of the state’s data reporting system.

item.title: Benson, James, Duggan grow money momentum in Michigan governor race
item.description: Democrat Jocelyn and John James are raising big bucks in their run for Michigan governor. But independent Mike Duggan raised more from donors than any other campaign last year.
